title: 11 Best AI App Builders for Turning Claude Artifacts Into Real Apps in 2027

body_markdown:
Claude Artifacts are brilliant for rapid prototyping. You describe what you want, and Claude generates interactive components, calculators, games, and utilities right in the chat. The problem is that artifacts were never designed to be production applications. Newer Artifacts can store up to 100 MB of data and 25,000 records on eligible Claude plans, while legacy Artifacts have a 20 MB storage limit. Artifacts do not support custom domains, but many shared links can be viewed without a Claude account.


According to the 2026 Stack Overflow survey,[65.9% of respondents](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2026/ai/data/ai-select) use AI coding assistants or coding agents at work. For non-technical founders, freelancers, and small business owners, however, the gap between generating a working prototype and launching a hosted application can still feel enormous. That gap is exactly what AI app builders address. Platforms like[Floot](https://floot.com/) let you rebuild an artifact's functionality as a hosted application with a database, authentication, payments, and your own domain.


This guide covers 11 AI app builders and deployment options that can help you move from artifact to a hosted app in 2027, compared by Claude integration, backend infrastructure, ease of use, and pricing accessibility.


## **Key Takeaways**


- **Connector-assisted app building:** Floot is a[full-stack app platform](https://floot.com/docs/getting-started/how-floot-works) with an MCP connector for Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. Supported building actions depend on each client's permissions.
- **Managed backend infrastructure:** Floot includes a[Postgres database](https://floot.com/docs/platform/database) , authentication, file storage, hosting, email, and payment workflows for applications with saved data and user accounts.
- **Building and pricing:** Floot is[free to start](https://floot.com/en/pricing) . Free includes 100 building actions daily and a one-time $3 hosting credit; Pro costs $25/month with 1,000 daily actions and a $10 monthly hosting allowance. Your eligible AI subscription is separate from Floot fees.
- **Mobile publishing:** The[current pricing plans](https://floot.com/en/pricing) include 2 mobile builds per month on Free, 12 on Pro, and unlimited builds on Power. Developer accounts and store approval are still required, and Google Play connection needs a paid Floot plan.
- **Ownership and export:** Floot users own their code and data on every plan.[Database export](https://floot.com/docs/faqs/code-data-and-exports) is available on all plans, while full-project ZIP downloads require a paid plan.


## **What to Look For in an AI App Builder**


Turning an artifact into a real app requires more than hosting static files. You need infrastructure that supports how production applications actually work.


A strong AI app builder for artifact conversion should address:


- **Backend infrastructure:** Managed databases, authentication systems, file storage, and serverless endpoints
- **Claude integration:** Direct MCP connector, manual code import, or standalone AI generation
- **Custom domains:** Ability to publish on your own domain with SSL certificates
- **Code ownership:** Whether you can export and self-host your project
- **Pricing transparency:** Clear costs without hidden per-token charges or usage surprises
- **Deployment speed:** How quickly you can go from artifact code to live URL
- **Mobile support:** Options for packaging web apps as native iOS and Android applications


The most practical choice depends on whether you need a full rebuild with backend services or a quick deployment of an already-working artifact.


## **1. Floot**


[Floot](https://floot.com/) is a full-stack app-building platform with an MCP connector that lets users create, edit, and publish applications through supported AI assistants. It is[Y Combinator-backed](https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/floot) and built for non-technical founders who want to ship production apps without hiring developers.


### **Primary Focus**


Floot addresses the gap between AI-generated prototypes and production infrastructure by working through supported assistants, including Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. The connected AI assistant handles development, while Floot provides managed databases, authentication, file storage, hosting, and live previews. Available actions depend on the client's connector permissions.


### **Organizational Fit**


Floot suits non-technical founders, small business owners, and operators who need working applications with user accounts, saved data, and hosting without configuring backend services themselves.


With an eligible existing Claude or ChatGPT subscription, ordinary connector building does not incur a second Floot AI build-credit charge. Floot plans, hosting usage, and optional AI features or image generation have separate allowances or charges.


### **Artifact-Relevant Capabilities**


- [MCP connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) for building through supported Claude, Codex, Cursor, and ChatGPT configurations
- Managed[Postgres database](https://floot.com/docs/platform/database) with SQL access and browser-based table view
- Built-in email/password and Google/Microsoft OAuth authentication
- File storage with CDN-backed delivery for assets
- Mobile app conversion with TestFlight and Google Play deployment support
- Custom domains on paid plans


### **Why It Leads for Artifact Conversion**


Floot works best for people using supported AI assistants to build full-stack applications with saved data and user accounts. It is[free to start](https://floot.com/en/pricing) : Free includes 100 daily build actions, 3,000 one-time starter AI credits, a one-time $3 hosting credit, and 2 mobile builds per month. Pro costs $25/month with 1,000 daily actions, 5,000 monthly AI credits, a $10 monthly hosting allowance, and 12 mobile builds. Power costs $100/month with 5,000 daily actions, 15,000 monthly AI credits, $25 monthly hosting, and unlimited mobile builds. Hosting beyond the included allowance is usage-billed. These Floot charges are separate from your connected AI subscription.


## **2. Lovable**


Lovable is a full-stack AI app builder with enterprise adoption across major brands. In November 2026, the company reported more than 70 million projects created and over 1 billion monthly visits to Lovable-built apps.


### **Primary Focus**


Lovable generates complete applications with backend infrastructure from natural language descriptions. The platform is positioned for teams that need enterprise-grade hosting, SSL, and security controls alongside AI-powered development.


### **Organizational Fit**


Lovable takes natural language descriptions and generates complete applications with backend infrastructure. It operates as a standalone platform rather than integrating into Claude conversations. Readers comparing workflows can review[Lovable alternatives](https://floot.com/blog/best-lovable-alternatives-in-2026-apps-that-can-actually-ship) .


### **Artifact-Relevant Capabilities**


- Full-stack generation from prompts with hosting included
- Stripe integration for one-time payments and subscriptions, subject to Stripe account and country availability
- Nearly 100 app connectors, according to Lovable's August 2026 update
- Analytics, security, and SEO features built in
- Web app deployment, including mobile-friendly applications and progressive web apps (PWAs)


### **Considerations**


Teams should evaluate whether Lovable's standalone workflow and enterprise feature set match their needs. Turning an existing Claude Artifact into a Lovable app may require recreating or adapting functionality rather than transferring a ready-to-run project.


## **3. Totalum**


Totalum is a full-stack AI app builder that generates Next.js and TypeScript applications. Source-code export and self-hosting are available on paid plans.


### **Primary Focus**


Totalum addresses artifact storage limitations by rebuilding the code into a deployable project with a managed SQL database and schema generation. You can use artifact code as a starting point and rebuild its functionality as a full application.


### **Organizational Fit**


Totalum converts artifact code into production-ready projects with backend infrastructure. The platform provides an MCP server for control from Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex.


### **Artifact-Relevant Capabilities**


- MCP server for control from Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex
- Next.js and TypeScript codebase with export on paid plans
- GitHub integration for version control
- SQLite database on Cloudflare D1 with schema generation
- Self-hosting supported after code export, with service dependencies handled separately


### **Considerations**


Totalum suits developers who want to download and manage their generated code. Paid plans start at $29/month, while a free tier is available for initial projects but does not include source-code export or GitHub sync.


## **4. Bolt.new**


Bolt.new by StackBlitz is a browser-based AI development environment for creating and deploying web applications.


### **Primary Focus**


Bolt runs a Node.js development environment in the browser without requiring a local installation. Users can generate, edit, preview, and deploy web application projects through its AI-assisted interface.


### **Organizational Fit**


Bolt provides a browser-based development environment rather than relying on the Floot MCP connector inside Claude. It is suited to building and editing project files, not simply publishing an unchanged Artifact.


### **Artifact-Relevant Capabilities**


- Browser-based development with no local installation
- AI-assisted code generation and editing in the browser
- Hosted app workflows with backend and authentication options
- Web previews and iterative interface development
- Project-level development beyond a single Artifact component


### **Considerations**


Teams already comfortable with browser-based coding may prefer Bolt, while those who want connector-driven app building can review these[Bolt alternatives](https://floot.com/blog/bolt-new-alternatives) . The choice depends on whether you prefer a separate browser development environment or editing through a connected assistant.


## **5. Replit**


Replit is a cloud-based AI development platform with millions of builders and enterprise customers including Zillow, Gusto, and Databricks.


### **Primary Focus**


Replit offers Free Mode for initial brainstorming and development within plan-specific allowances. Its intelligent model routing automatically selects a model for each task; in company testing, routing matched the previous Max Mode's output quality at 65% lower cost.


### **Organizational Fit**


Replit provides full-stack infrastructure with zero setup for auth, database, and hosting. The platform offers flexibility across multiple plan tiers.


### **Artifact-Relevant Capabilities**


- Free Mode for initial development within plan-specific allowances
- Full-stack infrastructure with zero setup for auth, database, and hosting
- 100+ integrations including OpenAI, Stripe, and Google Workspace
- Multi-user collaboration and project sharing
- $100 credit toward powerful models on Pro plan


### **Considerations**


Replit Core costs $18/month and Pro costs $90/month when billed annually, compared with $20/month and $100/month on monthly billing. Teams should compare the model-use credits and collaboration allowances included in each plan.


## **6. MindStudio**


MindStudio is a no-code AI workflow builder with access to 200+ AI models including Claude.


### **Primary Focus**


MindStudio is better suited to recreating an artifact's functionality as an AI workflow than importing and hosting the artifact as a full-stack web application. The platform supports 1,000+ integrations with tools like HubSpot, Airtable, Slack, and Google Workspace.


### **Organizational Fit**


MindStudio works well when your artifact needs to evolve into multi-step workflows with external integrations. The platform is model-agnostic rather than optimized specifically for Claude integration.


### **Artifact-Relevant Capabilities**


- Model-agnostic platform supporting 200+ AI models
- Multi-channel deployment across web, mobile, and Slack
- Persistent data storage and real-time external data connections
- No-code interface for non-technical users
- 1,000+ integrations with external tools


### **Considerations**


MindStudio works best when your artifact needs to connect with external tools and data sources. Its workflow-oriented approach is less direct for users who simply want to host an existing React Artifact unchanged.


## **7. InstaPods**


InstaPods is a deployment service designed specifically for Claude Artifacts, offering one-paste deployment from artifact source to live URL.


### **Primary Focus**


InstaPods focuses on deployment. You copy your artifact source, paste it, and deploy it to a live URL. Actual deployment time depends on the artifact and any additional configuration required.


### **Organizational Fit**


For artifact conversion, InstaPods publishes existing code rather than rebuilding its functionality as a new full-stack application. Its standalone deployment can remove the Anthropic branding bar from published artifacts.


### **Artifact-Relevant Capabilities**


- One-paste deployment from artifact code
- Automatic HTTPS with SSL on custom domains
- Removes Anthropic branding bar from published artifacts
- CLI tool for scripting and batch deployments
- Flat pricing with no bandwidth charges


### **Considerations**


The Launch plan costs $3/month and the Build plan costs $7/month, with a one-time $10 credit when adding a payment card. The Build plan includes database options, whereas Launch is suited to smaller static projects.


## **8. Netlify**


Netlify is a web development and deployment platform that supports publishing Claude-generated websites and applications.


### **Primary Focus**


Netlify provides a straightforward route from Claude Artifacts to a hosted website. Static HTML artifacts can be deployed through Netlify Drop, while React-based artifacts may require a build step or a compatible project setup before deployment.


### **Organizational Fit**


Netlify is useful when you already have working artifact code and need hosting. More complex applications may require additional configuration for databases, authentication, and backend services.


### **Artifact-Relevant Capabilities**


- Drag-and-drop deployment for static HTML artifacts
- Hosting for React and other web applications
- Custom domains and HTTPS support
- Git-based deployment workflows
- Integration with Claude and other AI coding tools


### **Considerations**


React-based artifacts may require a build step before deployment. Claude-specific runtime features may also need changes before the application works independently.


## **9. Base44**


Base44 is a no-code AI app builder optimized for non-technical founders who need fast MVP validation.


### **Primary Focus**


Base44 generates applications from natural language descriptions with automatic backend and database setup. It is positioned for users who want to validate ideas without touching code.


### **Organizational Fit**


Base44 operates as a standalone platform designed for non-technical users who need fast MVP validation. Users describe the app they want and then refine it through Base44’s own building interface, rather than working inside Claude.


### **Artifact-Relevant Capabilities**


- Natural language app generation
- Automatic backend and database configuration
- Designed for non-technical users
- Fast MVP validation without hiring engineers
- No code access required


### **Considerations**


Teams should evaluate whether its no-code approach matches their needs compared with MCP-connected options that work inside Claude conversations. Existing Artifact logic may need to be recreated in Base44 rather than deployed unchanged.


## **10. claude-artifact-runner (Open Source)**


claude-artifact-runner is a free, open-source Vite-based project for running React Claude Artifacts locally or on a server.


### **Primary Focus**


For developers who want control without paying for the runner itself, this project supplies a preconfigured environment for React Artifact code. You still need to copy in the component, install dependencies, and arrange hosting, which may involve ongoing costs.


### **Organizational Fit**


This option is designed for developers comfortable with technical workflows and self-hosting. It provides a Git-friendly project structure with common Artifact dependencies.


### **Artifact-Relevant Capabilities**


- Provides a Vite project for running React Artifact code
- Includes dependencies such as Lucide, Recharts, and Tailwind
- Uses a project structure suitable for Git version control
- Full control over deployment destination


### **Considerations**


This option requires technical knowledge, including installing packages and configuring a deployment environment. The project is free to use, but hosting and ongoing maintenance remain your responsibility.


## **11. ChatGPT Sites**


ChatGPT Sites lets users create, host, and publish interactive websites and lightweight applications directly through ChatGPT and Codex.


### **Primary Focus**


ChatGPT Sites is useful when you want to recreate a Claude Artifact's functionality as a hosted website or lightweight app using ChatGPT. It supports conversational building, live previews, and publishing without setting up a separate deployment service.


### **Organizational Fit**


ChatGPT Sites is not an MCP infrastructure connector for Claude. It provides its own building and hosting workflow inside ChatGPT.


### **Artifact-Relevant Capabilities**


- Website and lightweight app generation through ChatGPT
- Built-in hosting and shareable URLs
- Database storage and file uploads
- Access controls and supported sign-in options
- Custom domain support
- Conversational editing and deployment


### **Considerations**


ChatGPT Sites is available on eligible paid ChatGPT plans. Building and editing count toward Codex usage, while hosting and storage have separate allowances and limits. Hosting charges beyond plan allowances are scheduled to start January 1, 2027. It is worth considering for lightweight web applications, dashboards, and internal tools. For users who want to keep building through Claude or another supported MCP client while using managed full-stack infrastructure and mobile-app publishing workflows, Floot provides a different approach.


## **Why Floot Leads for Claude Artifact Conversion**


Floot is a full-stack app-building platform with an[MCP connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) for supported AI assistants. You can describe your Claude Artifact's functionality, and the connected assistant can rebuild it as a hosted Floot application instead of automatically importing its original code. Available building capabilities depend on the client's connector permissions.


- **Managed infrastructure:** Postgres database, authentication, file storage, CDN, and hosting.
- **Flexible building:** Use supported Claude, Codex, Cursor, or ChatGPT configurations and an eligible existing AI subscription.
- **Publishing options:** Live URLs, paid-plan custom domains, payments, and iOS and Android build workflows.


The pricing model also matters. Floot offers daily building-action allowances, while hosting beyond included amounts is usage-billed. Ordinary connector building does not incur a second Floot AI build-credit charge; optional AI features have separate credit rules. For non-technical founders, the[artifacts versus hosted apps](https://floot.com/blog/claude-artifacts-vs-a-real-hosted-app-what-s-the-difference) comparison explains how a prototype can become an application with its own logins, saved data, and domain.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What is the main limitation of Claude Artifacts for production use?**


Legacy Claude Artifacts have a 20 MB storage limit, while newer Artifacts support up to 100 MB and 25,000 saved records. Artifacts do not support custom domains, and many shared links work without a Claude account. They can store persistent data but do not replace a separately hosted full-stack application with customizable accounts, payments, and backend infrastructure. Floot explains the[Artifact hosting differences](https://floot.com/blog/claude-artifacts-vs-a-real-hosted-app-what-s-the-difference) .


### **Can I turn a Claude Artifact into a mobile app?**


Yes, by rebuilding its functionality through a platform such as Floot, which supports iOS and Android builds. The[Floot pricing plans](https://floot.com/en/pricing) include 2 monthly mobile builds on Free, 12 on Pro, and unlimited builds on Power. You still need the relevant Apple and Google developer accounts; Google Play connection requires a paid Floot plan. App-store testing and submissions do not guarantee approval.


### **What are build actions and how do they affect pricing?**


[Build actions](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-actions) are operations a connected AI assistant runs through Floot, such as reading files, editing code, and testing changes. Floot's daily allowances are 100 on Free, 1,000 on Pro, and 5,000 on Power; failed actions do not count. Ordinary connector building uses the eligible assistant's subscription rather than a second Floot AI build-credit charge, while hosting and optional AI features have separate costs.


### **Do I own the code from apps built with AI app builders?**


Ownership varies by platform. Floot says users own their project code, app data, and intellectual property on every plan. Database export is available on all plans, while full project ZIP download requires a paid plan, as described in its[code export guide](https://floot.com/docs/faqs/code-data-and-exports) . Running exported code elsewhere may require configuring hosting, authentication, and other services.


### **Should I use a full-stack builder or a deployment-only tool?**


It depends on your Artifact. If it already works and you only need hosting with a custom domain, deployment tools such as InstaPods or Netlify can provide a direct route. If the application needs a database, authentication, payments, or other backend functionality, rebuilding it on a full-stack platform such as Floot, Lovable, or Totalum can reduce separate infrastructure setup.
